QASHANI:92:13-17/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:92:13-17/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:92:13-17/r4.claim: Only the most wretched, lacking readiness and sharing in shirk, enters it: the one who denies God and turns away stubbornly.
QASHANI:92:13-17/r4.anchor: العديم الاستعداد، الخبيث الجوهر، المشرك بالله في المواقف الأربعة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.claim: Verses 15–21 explain the traits of those cast into Hell and those shielded from it, together with their reward.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.anchor: An explanation of the character of people who will be thrown into Hell and those who will be shielded from it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.claim: The warning addresses Quraysh: persistent deniers of truth face the blazing fire, while those who spend to attain purity are protected from it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.anchor: people who spend their wealth to attain purity will be shielded from this fire.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4.claim: The contrast is between rejecters of God’s Messengers and believers, not degrees of wickedness or piety; conclusive warning leaves Messenger-rejecters no legitimate excuse, making them the most wretched.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4.anchor: less pious and the more pious

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the superlatives mark two great opposing figures as if Hell were made only for the worst and Paradise only for the most pious; some identify them as Abū Jahl or Umayya and Abū Bakr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r12.anchor: الآية واردة في الموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين وعظيم من المؤمنين

FARRA:v3p272/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p272/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p272/r2.claim: Only the person known by God to be wretched will enter the Fire.
FARRA:v3p272/r2.anchor: وقوله عز وجل: لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى (15) . إلا من كان شقيا في علم الله.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r6.claim: The warning to Mecca is of a flaming fire; only the wretched, who denied the Messenger and turned from faith, enters it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r6.anchor: {فأنذرتكم} يا أهل مكة، {نارا تلظى لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى} أي: تتلظى، يعني تتوقد وتتوهج

BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r3.claim: Only the most wretched unbeliever abides in the Fire; a sinful believer may enter without remaining there.
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r3.anchor: { لا يصلها } لا يلزمها مقاسيا شدتها. { إلا الأشقى } إلا الكافر

BINTSHATI:v2p113/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p113/r2.speaker: المفسرون
BINTSHATI:v2p113/r2.claim: Some interpret la yaslaha as meaning that only the most wretched warms himself by the Fire.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r2.claim: Only the most wretched, meaning the unbeliever, undergoes the fire permanently; a sinful believer may enter but will not remain there.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r2.anchor: فإن الفاسق وإن دخلها لا يكون ذلك له على طريق اللزوم

NAHHAS:v5p243/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p243/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
NAHHAS:v5p243/r4.claim: He uses al-ashqā as a synonym for al-shaqī.
NAHHAS:v5p243/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة الأشقى بمعنى الشقي

NAHHAS:v5p243/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p243/r5.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p243/r5.claim: He takes al-ashqā as the person who is most wretched in God's knowledge.
NAHHAS:v5p243/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء الأشقى الشقي في علم الله سبحانه

NAHHAS:v5p243/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p243/r6.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p243/r6.claim: Alternatively, only the worst among the people of Hell enters it; since they are unbelievers, this indicates that sinful believers may also enter Hell.
NAHHAS:v5p243/r6.anchor: وأشقى أهل النار الكفار ودل بهذا على أن غير الكفار يدخلون النار بذنوبهم

DURR-FULL:v8p536/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r7.claim: The Prophet said all would enter Paradise except those who refuse; when asked who refuses, he recited ‘the one who denied and turned away.’
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r7.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن أبي هريرة

DURR-FULL:v8p536/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r8.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r8.claim: He said everyone in the community enters Paradise except one who rebels against God like a bad camel against its owner, citing the description of the wretched denier.
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r8.anchor: وأخرج سعيد بن منصور وابن أبي حاتم وابن المنذر والطبراني وابن مردويه عن أبي أمامة

DURR-FULL:v8p536/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r9.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r9.claim: The Prophet said everyone enters Paradise except one who bolts from God as a camel bolts from its owner.
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r9.anchor: وأخرج أحمد والحاكم عن أبي أمامة الباهلي

DURR-FULL:v8p536/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r10.claim: The Prophet said everyone enters Paradise except the one who refuses; whoever obeys him enters, and whoever disobeys has refused.
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r10.anchor: وأخرج أحمد والبخاري عن أبي هريرة

DURR-FULL:v8p536/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r11.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r11.claim: The Prophet said only the wretched enter the Fire; the wretched are those who neither obey God nor refrain from disobedience.
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r11.anchor: وأخرج أحمد وابن مردويه عن أبي أمامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r3.claim: The clause excluding all but the most wretched from this particular Fire is a second descriptor or a circumstantial clause; this is the Fire prepared for disbelievers, as in al-Baqara, and the next verse confirms it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r3.anchor: وهذه نار خاصة أعدت للكافرين فهي التي في قوله : { فاتقوا النار التي وقودها الناس والحجارة أعدت للكافرين } ( البقرة : 24 ) والقرينة على ذلك قوله : { وسيجنبها الأتقى } الآية .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says this verse prompted the Murjiʾa to claim that only unbelievers enter Hell; Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects the generalization because this is one specific Fire and Hell has levels, including the lowest for hypocrites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r4.anchor: وذكر القرطبي أن أبا إسحاق الزجاج قال : هذه الآية التي من أجلها قال أهل الإرجاء بالإرجاء فزعموا : أن لا يدخل النار إلا كافر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r5.claim: The most wretched are explicitly identified as those who denied the Messenger and turned away from the Quran; in the early Islamic audience this described the disbelievers, while the most God-fearing are named to complete the contrast.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r5.anchor: وقد أتبع { الأشقى } بصفة { الذي كذب وتولى } لزيادة التنصيص على أنهم المقصود بذلك فإنهم يعلمون أنهم كذبوا الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وتولوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r6.claim: الأشقى and الأتقى mean the most wretched and most devout in degree, a common intensifying usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r6.anchor: و { الأشقى } و { الأتقى } مراد بهما : الشديد الشقاء والشديد التقوى ومثله كثير في الكلام .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r1.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r1.claim: Al-Qurṭubī reports that ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wept while reciting the threat of blazing Fire at Maghrib, could not continue, and switched to another surah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r1.anchor: وذكر القرطبي : أن مالكا قال : صلى بنا عمر بن عبد العزيز المغرب فقرأ { والليل إذا يغشى } فلما بلغ : { فأنذرتكم نارا تلظى } وقع عليه البكاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r2.claim: The relative clauses describing the most wretched and most God-fearing indicate that their deeds cause the respective verdicts; the two superlatives also form a near-rhyme.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r2.anchor: ووصف { الأشقى } بصلة { الذي كذب وتولى } ، ووصف { الأتقى } بصلة { الذي يؤتى ماله يتزكى } للإيذان بأن للصلة تسببا في الحكم .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r15.claim: Arabic may use the superlative form afʿal to mean an emphatic active participle, as in Tarafa's poem.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r15.anchor: والعرب تجعل أفعل في موضع فاعل مبالغة كما قال طرفة

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r2.claim: He gives three explanations of “none enters it but the most wretched”: only one matching the stated traits approaches it; the Fire is named for its majority and intended occupants; or “only” signals the most deserving, without excluding others.
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r2.anchor: ذكر هذه الوجوه الثلاثة أبو مسلم

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r3.claim: The exclusionary reading cannot mean that no sinful person enters Hell: that would contradict consensus, encourage or permit sin, and conflict with the threat against the miser and sinner.
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r3.anchor: لوجب القطع على أن الفاسق لا يدخل النار، وفيه خلاف الإجماع، وإغراء بالمعاصي

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r4.claim: Another explanation supplies an ellipsis: “the most wretched, and whoever is like him among the sinners.”
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r4.anchor: كأنه قيل: الأشقى، ومن جرى مجراه من العصاة

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r5.claim: A further view says some disbelievers enter the Fire without having committed each specified act of denial, miserliness, and turning away; the author says the first explanation is best.
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r5.anchor: أن من الكفار من يدخلها، وإن لم يكذب، ولم يبخل، ولم يتول

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r6.claim: He prefers the first of the explanations of who enters the Fire.

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r1.speaker: several commentators
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r1.claim: Commentators tell of a Medinan palm owner who snatched fallen dates from a poor family's children and refused the Prophet's offer of a Paradise palm; another man paid forty palms, donated the tree, and the Prophet gave it to the family. The refusal maps to vv. 15–16, the gift to vv. 18–21.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r1.anchor: Several commentators say that the whole of this sūrah was revealed in reference to a Muslim of Madinah who had a palm tree

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r2.claim: If this is an early Makkan sūrah, the palm-tree story likely is not its occasion; the verses instead generally condemn those who rejected Muhammad as prophet.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r2.anchor: If, however, this is an early Makkan sūrah, as some maintain

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura develops two antitheses: behavior and recompense for the saved and damned, first in verses 5–13 and then in verses 14–21.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.anchor: Es folgen zwei Antithesen (V. 5–13 und V. 14–21), welche die Verhaltensweisen und Jenseitsschicksale von Seligen und Verdammten miteinander kontrastieren

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.claim: The final stanza reverses the earlier order of saved and damned; the outer blessed sections are linked by ittaqā in verse 5 and ʾatqā in verse 17.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.anchor: Zum einen wird die Reihenfolge Seliger – Verdammter (V. 5–7 und V. 8–11) jetzt invertiert (V. 14–16 Verdammter, V. 17–20 Seliger)

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.claim: The stanza halves mirror one another: earlier behavior lists precede reward or warning, while the final warning and promise precede each group's worldly conduct.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.anchor: In V. 5–7 und V. 8–11 ging zunächst ein Tugend- bzw. Lasterkatalog voraus, auf den dann jeweils ein Drohwort bzw. eine Verheißung folgten

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r3.claim: The second antithesis concretizes the first: verse 14 resolves the enigmatic threat of verse 10 as the image of blazing Hell.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r4.claim: This movement from riddle to shocking disclosure resembles the teaching question and explicit Hell image in 104:4–7 and the eschatological resolution in 102:3–8.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r4.anchor: Eine analoge Sequenz aus Enigma und eschatologischer Auflösung liegt Q 102:3–8 zu Grunde

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r5.claim: The moral opposition is now named directly through the labels al-ašqā for the damned and al-atqā for the pious.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r5.anchor: insofern beide nicht nur durch Relativsätze (man …) qualifiziert, sondern mit prägnanten Bezeichnungen (V. 15: al-ʾašqā, V. 17: al-ʾatqā) belegt werden

TABATABAI:92:15-20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:15-20/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:15-20/r1.claim: “Only the most wretched enters it” denies lasting residence in the Fire to anyone but unbelievers; it does not deny that sinful believers may enter temporarily.
TABATABAI:92:15-20/r1.anchor: الآية إنما تنفي عن غير الكافر الخلود فيها دون أصل الدخول

THALABI:v10p218#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p218#2/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v10p218#2/r3.claim: He reads that none enters Paradise except one who refuses, explaining that the refuser is the one who lies and turns away.
THALABI:v10p218#2/r3.anchor: قرأ أبو هريرة: ليدخلن الجنة إلا من يأبى

ELMALILI:92:12-21/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r6.claim: The most wretched is the disbeliever, defined as one who denies God's guidance and turns away from the truth.
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r6.anchor: “Eşkā”dan murad kâfir olduğu anlatılmak için şununla beyan ve tefsir olunmuştur

ELMALILI:92:12-21/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r7.claim: A sinner who turns away without denying is wretched but not the most wretched; even if he enters the Fire, he does not remain there.
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r7.anchor: Tekzib etmeksizin i‘râz eden fâsık ise en şakī değil şakīdir, o ateşe girerse de yaslanıp kalmaz.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.claim: Others say verses 5–19 were revealed about Abu Bakr; regardless of a specific occasion, the message and rulings are general.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.anchor: bazıları ise 5-19. âyetlerin (bk. Elmalılı, VIII, 5881), müşriklerin işkence ettiği köleleri satın alıp âzat ederek hürriyetlerine kavuşturan Hz. Ebû Bekir hakkında indiğini söylemişlerdir. Âyetler böyle bir özel olay üzerine gelmiş olsa da, hükümleri ve mesajları geneldir

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3441#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3441#3/r1.speaker: أبو أمامة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3441#3/r1.claim: Abu Umama says no one of this community enters Hell except one who flees from God; the one who enters is the most wretched, who denied Muhammad's message and turned away from him.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3441#3/r1.anchor: عن أبي امامة قال : لا يبقى أحد من هذه الامة الا ادخله الله الجنة الا من شرد علي الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#4/r1.claim: The most wretched who enters this Fire is the polytheist.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#4/r1.anchor: لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى يعني المشرك

JISHUMI:v10p7444/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r10.claim: Ashqā and atqā are elatives from shaqī and taqī; tajannub means setting something apart, so the most pious is pictured far from Hell and on Paradise's side.
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r10.anchor: والأشقى: أفعل من الشقي، والأكبر من الكبير، وكذلك الأتقى من التقى.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r1.speaker: أبو الزبير
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r1.claim: Abu al-Zubayr reads the verb with an extra ta: tatalaẓẓā.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r2.claim: The exclusive descriptions pair two eminent opponents and intensify their contrast; they do not mean only the most wicked burns or only the most devout escapes.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r2.anchor: قلت : الآية واردة في الموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r3.claim: The two figures contrasted are said to be Abu Jahl or Umayya ibn Khalaf and Abu Bakr.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r3.anchor: وقيل : هما أبو جهل أو أمية بن خلف ، وأبو بكر

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r12.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r12.claim: He says the person lied about God's Book and turned away from God's obedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r12.anchor: وتولى عن طاعة الله , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r13.claim: A second interpretation says the person lied about the Messenger and turned away from obeying him.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r14.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r14.claim: One reading says no one at God's side has a favor to repay: rather, perform an act seeking God's face and earn its reward.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r15.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r15.claim: They apply the verse to Bilal: Abu Bakr's purchase and freeing of him repaid no prior favor; he acted only to seek God's face.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r16.claim: The promised satisfaction may come from the abundance of what is given or from being content with what is given, since a content person obeys God more.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r16.anchor: بما أعطيه لقناعته , لأن من قنع بغير عطاء

NASAFI-FULL:v4p344/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344/r1.claim: Only the most wretched unbeliever, who denied the messengers and turned away from faith, enters the Fire eternally.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344/r1.anchor: ﴿ لا يصلاها ﴾ لا يدخلها للخلود فيها ﴿ إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى ﴾

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r4.claim: La yaslaha means the person does not experience its heat.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r4.anchor: { لا يصلاها } أي لا يجد صلاها وهو حرها

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r7.speaker: مكحول، أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r7.claim: Makhul transmits from Abu Hurayra that everyone enters Paradise except one who refuses; the refuser denied and turned away.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r7.anchor: وروى مكحول عن أبي هريرة قال: كل يدخل الجنة إلا من أباها

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r9.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r9.claim: Al-Farra says ashqa is whoever God knew would be wretched.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r9.anchor: وقال الفراء: «إلا الأشقى» إلا من كان شقيا في علم الله

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r10.speaker: الضحاك، ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r10.claim: They identify the wretched one as Umayya ibn Khalaf and those like him who denied Muhammad.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r10.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال: «لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى» أمية بن خلف ونظراؤه

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r15.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r15.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the Murjiites wrongly infer that only unbelievers enter Hell: this names one particular fire, while Hell has levels and other promised punishments remain possible.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r15.anchor: أبا إسحاق الزجاج يقول: هذه الآية التي من أجلها قال أهل الإرجاء بالإرجاء، فزعموا أنه لا يدخل النار إلا كافر

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r1.claim: If every non-polytheist were exempt from punishment, the promise to forgive lesser sins “for whom He wills” at 4:48 would be pointless.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r1.anchor: فلو كان كل من لم يشرك لم يعذب، لم يكن في قوله: { ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشآء } فائدة

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads a rhetorical contrast between the worst disbeliever, uniquely associated with Fire, and the most pious believer, uniquely associated with Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r2.anchor: الزمخشري: الآية واردة في الموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين وعظيم من المؤمنين

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r3.claim: Some identify the worst one as Abu Jahl or Umayya ibn Khalaf.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: هما أبو جهل أو أمية بن خلف

QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.claim: An alternative contextual account identifies the giver as Abu al-Dahdah and the miser as the Ansari palm owner; it maps ease to Paradise, hardship to Hell, and death to loss of wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.anchor: { فأما من أعطى واتقى } يعني أبا الدحداح. { وصدق بالحسنى } أي بالثواب

QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r2.claim: In that account, the wretched one is a Khazraji hypocrite who died persisting in hypocrisy.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r2.anchor: { لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى } يعني بذلك الخزرجي وكان منافقا، فمات على نفاقه

QUTB-ZILAL:92:15/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:15/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:15/r1.claim: Only the most wretched of all servants undergoes the blazing fire; Qutb underscores that no greater misery is imaginable.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:15/r1.anchor: أشقى العباد جميعا . وهل بعد الصلي في النار شقوة

RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r1.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r1.claim: The Qadi objects that other sinners would be excluded from Hell; Razi replies that every disbeliever denied the prophet and turned away from examining his signs, so all disbelievers fit the description.
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r1.anchor: أن كل كافر لا بد وأن يكون مكذبا للنبي في دعواه

RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r2.claim: The claim that the verse encourages sin fails: present-world blame and God's withholding honor and reward can deter, and punishment may take other forms.
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r2.anchor: يكفي في الزجر عن المعصية حصول الذم في العاجل

RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r4.claim: The Qadi's claim that the warning names only a particular blazing fire is weak, since the phrase can describe all Hell; another verse calls it a blaze that strips the skin.
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r4.anchor: لأن قوله : { نارا تلظى } يحتمل أن يكون ذلك صفة لكل النيران

RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r5.claim: Reading 'most wretched' as merely more deserving of Hell abandons the apparent meaning without evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r5.anchor: لأنه ترك للظاهر من غير دليل

RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r6.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r6.claim: Al-Wahidi says yaṣlāhā means enduring the Fire's heat: unbelievers remain there, whereas a sinful believer either never enters or later escapes.
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r6.anchor: ما ذكره الواحدي وهو أن معنى : { لا يصلاها }

RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r7.claim: Alternatively, the general wording can be qualified by verses warning sinful believers of punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r7.anchor: أن يخص عموم هذا الظاهر بالآيات الدالة على وعيد الفساق

SAMIN-DURR:92:15/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:15/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:92:15/r1.claim: One view takes ashqā and atqā to mean simply wretched and pious, without comparison, since the fire and its avoidance are not exclusive to the most extreme cases.
SAMIN-DURR:92:15/r1.anchor: قيل: الأشقى والأتقى بمعنى الشقي والتقي ولا تفضيل فيهما؛ لأن النار ليست مختصة بالأكثر شقاء

SAMIN-DURR:92:15/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:15/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:92:15/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī keeps the comparative force and explains the wording as a balance between an eminent unbeliever and believer, hyperbolically as if the fire and paradise were made for each alone; he identifies them as Abū Jahl or Umayya ibn Khalaf and Abū Bakr.
SAMIN-DURR:92:15/r2.anchor: الآية واردة في لموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين وعظيم من المؤمنين، فأريد أن يبالغ في صفتيهما

TAB:92:15/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:15/r1.speaker: author
TAB:92:15/r1.claim: Only the most wretched enters and burns in the Fire: the one who denied God's signs, turned away, and did not affirm them.
TAB:92:15/r1.anchor: لا يدخلها فيصلى بسعيرها إلاّ الأشقى ،   الذي كذّبَ وتَوَلّى يقول :  الذي كذّب بآيات ربه

TAB:92:15/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:15/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB:92:15/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra says all will enter Paradise except whoever refuses, and cites the description of the one who denied and turned away.
TAB:92:15/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ،   قال :  لتدخُلنّ الجنة إلاّ من يأبى ،   قالوا :  يا أبا هريرة

TAB:92:15/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:15/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB:92:15/r3.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the most wretched as the polytheist; Muʿadh, rather than al-Hasan, adds ‘who denied and turned away.’
TAB:92:15/r3.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله :  لا يَصْلاها إلاّ الأشْقَى قال مُعاذ :  الذي كذّب وتولى

TAB:92:15/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:15/r4.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB:92:15/r4.claim: Some Arab grammarians say takdhīb can mean failing in obedience: like a fighter who ‘lies’ by retreating, without an explicit denial.
TAB:92:15/r4.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية يقول :  لم يكن كذب بردّ ظاهر ،   ولكن قصّر عما أمر به

TAB:92:15/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:15/r5.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB:92:15/r5.claim: They cite an Arab expression meaning fighters did not retreat, and compare it with the Qur'anic description of the Event as having no falsehood.
TAB:92:15/r5.anchor: وذُكر أنه سمع بعض العرب يقول :  ليس لحدّهم مكذوبة ،   بمعنى :  أنهم إذا لقوا

TAB:92:16/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:16/r1.speaker: author
TAB:92:16/r1.claim: Only the most wretched enters and burns in the Fire: the one who denied God's signs, turned away, and did not affirm them.
TAB:92:16/r1.anchor: لا يدخلها فيصلى بسعيرها إلاّ الأشقى ،   الذي كذّبَ وتَوَلّى يقول :  الذي كذّب بآيات ربه

TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r4.claim: Only the most wretched enters the blaze: the person who denied God's signs and turned away.
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r4.anchor: لا يدخلها فيصلى بسعيرها إلا الأشقى {الذي كذب وتولى} [الليل: 16]

TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r5.claim: Abū Hurayra says everyone will enter Paradise except those who refuse, and identifies the refuser by the description of the one who denied and turned away.
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: لتدخلن الجنة إلا من يأبى، قالوا: يا أبا هريرة: ومن يأبى أن يدخل الجنة؟

TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r6.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the most wretched as the polytheist.
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r6.anchor: قال معاذ: الذي كذب وتولى، ولم يقله الحسن، قال: المشرك

TABATABAI:92:13-16/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r6.claim: Al-ashqā means any unbeliever who denies the true call and turns away, not the single most wretched person of all humanity; eternal afterlife misery exceeds temporary worldly suffering.
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r6.anchor: والمراد بالأشقى مطلق الكافر الذي يكفر بالتكذيب والتولي فإنه أشقى من سائر من شقي في دنياه

TABATABAI:92:13-16/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r7.claim: Ṣaly al-nār means adhering to and remaining with the fire, implying permanence, which God decreed for unbelievers.
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r7.anchor: والمراد بصلي النار اتباعها ولزومها فيفيد معنى الخلود

THALABI:v10p220/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r1.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v10p220/r1.claim: A man refused the Prophet’s offer of a date palm in Paradise for his palm that dropped fruit into a neighbor’s yard; Abū al-Daḥdāḥ bought and donated it, and the Prophet transferred it to the neighbor. The account identifies them with the surah’s contrasting figures.
THALABI:v10p220/r1.anchor: عطاء قال: كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة، وكان له جار، فكان يسقط من بلحها في دار جاره

THALABI:v10p220/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p220/r3.claim: The palm’s owner represents the miser who deems himself self-sufficient and denies reward; he is eased toward Hell and is the “most wretched” who enters the blazing fire.
THALABI:v10p220/r3.anchor: وأما من بخل واستغنى يعني الأنصاري وكذب بالحسنى يعني الثواب فسنيسره للعسرى يعني النار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p86#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p86#2/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p86#2/r1.claim: Al-ashqā means whoever was wretched in God's knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p86#2/r1.anchor: {لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى} يعني إلا من كان شقيا في علم الله. قاله الفراء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p86#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p86#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p86#2/r2.claim: The referent is Umayya ibn Khalaf and his peers, who denied Muḥammad and the prophets before him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p86#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يريد أمية بن خلف، ونظراءه الذين كذبوا محمدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p86#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p86#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p86#2/r3.claim: Al-ashqā means the polytheist, as the next verse indicates.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p86#2/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: يعني المشرك (¬1)، ويدل عليه قوله:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r2.claim: The restriction to the denier applies to a particular level of Hell; its inhabitants occupy different levels.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r2.anchor: أحدهما: أن هذا ورد في درك مخصوص من أدراك جهنم؛ لا يحله إلا) (¬4) من كان بهذه الصفة، وهي: دركات، ولأهل النار منها منازل، (وهذا قول أبي إسحاق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r3.claim: Another answer is that mention of sinful non-polytheists is abbreviated; yuslīhā means enduring the fire's heat and does not itself imply abiding eternally, which only applies to the denying polytheist.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r3.anchor: والثاني: أن هذا على الاختصار بحذف ذكر العصاة من غير المشركين، بدليل الآي الآخر، على أن معنى قوله: {لا يصلاها}

WAHIDI-QT:92:15/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:15/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:15/r1.claim: Only a disbeliever enters that fire.
WAHIDI-QT:92:15/r1.anchor: { لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى } لا يدخلها إلا الكافر { الذي كذب وتولى }

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:15:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:15:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:15:anmerkung/r1.claim: Al-ashqā is compared with 91:12 and 87:11, also Group II early-Makkan suras.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:15:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Vgl. 91:12 und 87:11 (beides Suren, die wie Q 92 zu Gruppe II der frühmekkanischen Verkündigungen gehören

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:14/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:14/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:14/r1.claim: Alongside showing people the right path, God warns through revelation and prophets against Hell, the consequence of following the wrong path.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:14/r1.anchor: yanlış yolda gitmenin sonucu olan cehenneme karşı da onları vahiy ve peygamberleri aracılığıyla uyarmıştır

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#4/r1.claim: The most wretched person who enters the fire is the unbeliever, more wretched than a sinful believer; the next verse's description makes this clear.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#4/r1.anchor: المراد به الكافر فإنه أشقى من الفاسق ويفصح بذلك وصفه بقوله تعالى

BURHAN:v4p90/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p90/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p90/r2.claim: In an adjective and similar constructions, agreement usually follows the preceding word’s form; agreement by meaning rather than form is rarer.
BURHAN:v4p90/r2.anchor: ثم الأكثر في نعتها وغيرها مرافقة اللفظ

ITQAN:v4p394/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p394/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p394/r12.claim: The most wretched person is Umayya ibn Khalaf.

NASHR:v2p81/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p81/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p81/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr opens the listed non-verse-final words on the routes that incline verse endings; for موسى he follows his usual between-vowels reading where imāla is transmitted.
NASHR:v2p81/r7.anchor: فإن أبا عمرو يفتح جميع ذلك من طريق المميلين له رءوس الآي لأنه ليس برأس آية

NASHR:v2p81/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p81/r8.speaker: الأزرق عن ورش
NASHR:v2p81/r8.claim: Al-Azraq’s Warsh routes through Ibn Ghalbūn and others open these non-final forms; al-Taysīr and related routes read them between vowels because they are written with yāʾ, including فأما من طغى.
NASHR:v2p81/r8.anchor: والأزرق عن ورش يفتح جميعه أيضا من طريق أبي الحسن بن غلبون، وأبيه عبد المنعم ومكي

ABUHAYYAN:92:15/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:15/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:92:15/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the passage as a comparison between two eminent figures, one among the polytheists and one among the believers, whose conditions are sharply opposed.
ABUHAYYAN:92:15/r1.anchor: الآية واردة في الموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين وعظيم من المؤمنين

ABUHAYYAN:92:15/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:15/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:92:15/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says calling him the most wretched and singling him out for burning magnifies the contrast, as though Hell were made only for him.
ABUHAYYAN:92:15/r2.anchor: فأريد أن يبالغ في صفتيهما المتناقضتين ، فقيل : { الأشقى } ، وجعل مختصاً بالصلى ، كأن النار لم تخلق إلا له

ABUHAYYAN:92:15/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:15/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:92:15/r3.claim: An unnamed view identifies the most wretched one as Abu Jahl or Umayya ibn Khalaf.
ABUHAYYAN:92:15/r3.anchor: وقيل : هما أبو جهل ، أو أمية بن خلف

ALUSI:92:15/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:15/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:15/r1.claim: Al-ashqā refers to the unbeliever, more wretched than the sinner; the next verse clarifies this with denial and turning away.
ALUSI:92:15/r1.anchor: المراد به الكافر فإنه أشقى من الفاسق ويفصح بذلك وصفه بقوله تعالى

ALUSI:92:17/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:17/r2.claim: The apparent restrictions seem to conflict: the first excludes sinful believers from Hell, while the second implies they are not kept away and so enter it.
ALUSI:92:17/r2.anchor: فالحصر السابق يقتضي أن لا يصلي المؤمن العاصي النار لأنه ليس داخلاً في عموم الأشقى

ALUSI:92:17/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r3.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI:92:17/r3.claim: Ibn al-Munīr transmits from language scholars that ṣalā is especially severe exposure to heat, like pushing a sheep between layers of embers; sinners may enter or suffer lesser punishment without that torment, while the most God-fearing do not enter.
ALUSI:92:17/r3.anchor: فقد نقل ابن المنير عن أئمة اللغة أن الصلى أن يحفروا حفيرة فيجمعوا فيها جمراً كثيراً

ALUSI:92:17/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:17/r4.claim: On the severe-torment interpretation, the first restriction denies only the most severe punishment to others, and the second does not require every less-pious person to enter or suffer it; they may receive lesser punishment.
ALUSI:92:17/r4.anchor: فيجوزو أن يدخلها ويعذب بها على وجهها عذاباً ليس بالأشد فلا مخالفة بين الحصرين

ALUSI:92:17/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI:92:17/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls the restrictions rhetorical hyperbole in a comparison of exemplary leaders among unbelievers and believers, not strict exclusions; al-Kashf praises this, but al-Alūsī notes its Muʿtazilite premise of eternal punishment for major sinners.
ALUSI:92:17/r5.anchor: قرر الزمخشري الاستشكال بأنه قد علم أن كل شقي بصلاها وكل تقي بجنيها

ALUSI:92:17/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r6.speaker: القاضي
ALUSI:92:17/r6.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues that the indefinite Hell in verse 15 could mean one level, so it need not say only unbelievers enter any Hell; al-Zamakhsharī objects that verse 17 then appears to keep all but the most pious from that level.

ALUSI:92:17/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI:92:17/r8.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra says the Prophet stated that only the wretched enter Hell; asked who they are, he replied they neither perform obedience nor avoid disobedience to God. Murjiʾites cite it, while Sunnis interpret sound reports alongside texts about punishment of major sinners.
ALUSI:92:17/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI:92:17/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:17/r9.claim: Another proposal treats the elatives as ordinary descriptors, a wretched person and a pious person; Ṭarafa uses wāḥid to mean alone, but this does not solve the restriction problem for unbelievers, poor pious people, children, and the mentally ill.
ALUSI:92:17/r9.anchor: وقيل في الجواب أن المراد بالأشقى والاتقى الشقي والتقي وشاع أفعل في مثل ذلك

ALUSI:92:17/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r10.speaker: طرفة
ALUSI:92:17/r10.claim: Ṭarafa's line uses wāḥid in the sense of alone, supporting the proposed non-elative reading.
ALUSI:92:17/r10.anchor: تمنى رجال أن أموت فإن أمت

ALUSI:92:17/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:17/r11.claim: After considering alternatives, al-Alūsī favors al-Kashshāf's rhetorical reading if one accepts descriptive implication, despite rejecting eternal damnation for sinful believers.
ALUSI:92:17/r11.anchor: نستحسن إن قلت بالمفهوم ما استحسنه صاحب الكشف مما مر عن الزمخشري

BAGHAWI:92:16/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:16/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:92:16/r1.claim: Only the most wretched enters that Fire.

BAYDAWI:92:15/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:15/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:15/r1.claim: Only the unbeliever remains in Hell and bears its severity; a sinful believer may enter without becoming one who stays there.
BAYDAWI:92:15/r1.anchor: إلا الكافر فإن الفاسق وإن دخلها لا يلزمها ولذلك سماه أشقى

BIQAI:92:15/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:15/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:15/r1.claim: The emphatic restriction continues the repeated distinction between the abodes of the virtuous and the wicked, denying that they are treated alike.
BIQAI:92:15/r1.anchor: تخصيص كل من المحسن والمسيء بداره بطريق الحصر

BIQAI:92:15/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:15/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:15/r2.claim: The most wretched is the unbeliever, who undergoes Hell's heat continuously; a sinful believer may enter it, but not in that abiding manner.
BIQAI:92:15/r2.anchor: فإن الفاسق وإن دخلها لا يكون ذلك له على طريق اللزوم

DURR:92:15/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:15/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR:92:15/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra says people will enter Paradise except one who refuses; when asked who refuses Paradise, he recites the next verse about the one who denied and turned away.
DURR:92:15/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : لتدخلن الجنة إلا من يأبى . قالوا ومن يأبى أن يدخل الجنة ؟ فقرأ { الذي كذب وتولى }

DURR:92:15/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:15/r2.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR:92:15/r2.claim: Abu Umama says everyone in this community will enter Paradise except one who strays from God like a bad camel from its master; he explains the wretched person as one who denied Muhammad's message and turned away.
DURR:92:15/r2.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال : لا يبقى أحد من هذه الأمة إلا أدخله الله الجنة إلا من شرد على الله كما يشرد البعير السوء

DURR:92:15/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:15/r3.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي
DURR:92:15/r3.claim: Abu Umama al-Bahili recalls the Prophet saying that all will enter Paradise except one who strays from God like a camel straying from its owner.
DURR:92:15/r3.anchor: عن أبي أمامة الباهلي أنه سئل عن ألين كلمة سمعها من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : سمعت رسول الله

DURR:92:15/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:15/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR:92:15/r4.claim: The Prophet says all his community will enter Paradise except one who refuses: obedience to him leads to Paradise, while disobedience is refusal.
DURR:92:15/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «كل أمتي تدخل الجنة يوم القيامة إلا من أبى

DURR:92:15/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:15/r5.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR:92:15/r5.claim: The Prophet says only a wretched person enters the Fire, defining the wretched as one who does no obedience for God and avoids no disobedience for God's sake.
DURR:92:15/r5.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «لا يدخل النار إلا شقيّ . قيل : ومن الشقي ؟

DURR:92:16/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:16/r2.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR:92:16/r2.claim: Abu Umama says all the community enter Paradise except one who bolts from God like a bad camel; he explains the verse as rejecting Muhammad’s message and turning away.
DURR:92:16/r2.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال : لا يبقى أحد من هذه الأمة إلا أدخله الله الجنة إلا من شرد على الله

IBNASHUR:92:15/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:15/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:15/r1.claim: The clause is either a second adjective or a circumstantial clause modifying the previously described fire.
IBNASHUR:92:15/r1.anchor: صفة ثانية أو حال من { ناراً } بعد أن وصفت

IBNASHUR:92:15/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:15/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:15/r2.claim: This is a particular fire prepared for unbelievers, as in Q 2:24; the following promise to spare the most pious clarifies the distinction.
IBNASHUR:92:15/r2.anchor: فاتقوا النار التي وقودها الناس والحجارة أعدت للكافرين

IBNASHUR:92:15/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:15/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
IBNASHUR:92:15/r3.claim: Al-Qurṭubī reports that al-Zajjāj identified this as the verse from which the Murjiʾa inferred that only an unbeliever enters the Fire.
IBNASHUR:92:15/r3.anchor: وذكر القرطبي أن أبا إسحاق الزجاج قال : هذه الآية التي من أجلها

IBNASHUR:92:15/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:15/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
IBNASHUR:92:15/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj rejects the Murjiʾa's inference: this is a particular fire entered only by the denier who turns away, while the Fire has ranks, including the hypocrites' lowest rank.
IBNASHUR:92:15/r4.anchor: وذكر القرطبي أن أبا إسحاق الزجاج قال : هذه الآية التي من أجلها قال أهل الإرجاء بالإرجاء

IBNASHUR:92:15/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:15/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:15/r5.claim: The contextual meaning is: none of you enter this fire except you.

IBNASHUR:92:15/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:15/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:15/r6.claim: The relative clause 'who denied and turned away' further specifies the intended people, who knew that they denied the Messenger and turned away from the Qurʾān.
IBNASHUR:92:15/r6.anchor: لزيادة التنصيص على أنهم المقصود بذلك فإنهم يعلمون أنهم كذبوا الرسول

IBNASHUR:92:15/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:15/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:15/r7.claim: At the rise of Islam, people fell into two groups, unbelievers or pious believers; converts had embraced Islam wholeheartedly and did not commit major sins, so the next verse states the converse explicitly.
IBNASHUR:92:15/r7.anchor: فقد كان الناس في زمن ظهور الإسلام أحد فريقين

IBNASHUR:92:15/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:15/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:15/r8.claim: Al-ashqā and al-atqā are intensive forms meaning the most wretched and the most pious.
IBNASHUR:92:15/r8.anchor: الشديد الشقاء والشديد التقوى ومثله كثير في الكلام

IBNASHUR:92:15/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:15/r9.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR:92:15/r9.claim: Al-Qurṭubī reports Mālik's account that ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wept while reciting the warning of the blazing Fire at Maghrib, could not continue, and changed sūras.
IBNASHUR:92:15/r9.anchor: أن مالكاً قال : صلى بنا عمر بن عبد العزيز المغرب فقرأ

IBNASHUR:92:15/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:15/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:15/r10.claim: The relative clauses describing the most wretched and most pious signal that their respective actions cause the stated outcome.
IBNASHUR:92:15/r10.anchor: للإيذان بأن للصلة تسببا في الحكم

IBNASHUR:92:15/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:15/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:15/r11.claim: Al-ashqā and al-atqā form a near-paronomasia (jinās muḍāriʿ).
IBNASHUR:92:15/r11.anchor: وبين { الأشقى } و{ الأتقى } محسن الجناس المضارع

IBNATIYYA:92:15/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:15/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:15/r1.claim: The negation of burning applies to eternal burning, not every brief or prolonged experience of the Fire.
IBNATIYYA:92:15/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى } أي { لا يصلاها } صلي خلود ،   ومن هنا ضلت المرجئة

IBNATIYYA:92:15/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:15/r2.speaker: المرجئة
IBNATIYYA:92:15/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects the Murjiʾa reading that the verse negates all burning, in both small and large measure.
IBNATIYYA:92:15/r2.anchor: ومن هنا ضلت المرجئة لأنها أخذت نفي الصلي مطلقاً في قليله وكثيره

IBNATIYYA:92:15/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:15/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:15/r3.claim: Al-ashqā here is the unbeliever, as the next verse identifies him as one who denied.
IBNATIYYA:92:15/r3.anchor: و { الأشقى } هنا ،   الكافر بدليل قوله الذي كذب

IBNATIYYA:92:15/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:15/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:15/r4.claim: Arabs can use an afʿal form in place of fāʿil for emphasis; the cited line attributed to Ṭarafa uses awḥad.
IBNATIYYA:92:15/r4.anchor: والعرب تجعل أفعل في موضع فاعل مبالغة كما قال طرفة : [ الطويل ] تمنى رجال أن أموت وإن أمت

IBNATIYYA:92:16/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:16/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:16/r1.claim: The repeated explanation limits the negation of burning to eternal burning, rather than denying every experience of the Fire.
IBNATIYYA:92:16/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى } أي { لا يصلاها } صلي خلود ،   ومن هنا ضلت المرجئة

IBNATIYYA:92:16/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:16/r2.speaker: المرجئة
IBNATIYYA:92:16/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the Murjiʾa erred by taking the negation to cover burning of any duration.
IBNATIYYA:92:16/r2.anchor: ومن هنا ضلت المرجئة لأنها أخذت نفي الصلي مطلقاً في قليله وكثيره

IBNKATHIR:92:15/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:15/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:92:15/r1.claim: Only the most wretched enters the Fire in a way that surrounds him on every side.
IBNKATHIR:92:15/r1.anchor: أي : لا يدخلها دخولا يحيط به من جميع جوانبه إلا الأشقى

IBNKATHIR:92:16/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:16/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:92:16/r2.claim: The Prophet says only a wretched person enters the Fire, defining that person as one who neither obeys God nor leaves a sin for His sake.
IBNKATHIR:92:16/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : " لا يدخل النار إلا شقي " . قيل : ومن الشقي ؟ قال : " الذي لا يعمل بطاعة ،   ولا يترك لله معصية "

KASHSHAF:92:15/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:15/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:15/r1.claim: The wording answers the objection that all wicked people enter Hell and all righteous people avoid it: the passage contrasts a leading disbeliever with a leading believer and hyperbolically singles each out as if Hell or Paradise were made just for him.
KASHSHAF:92:15/r1.anchor: الآية واردة في الموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين

KASHSHAF:92:17/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:17/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:17/r1.claim: The most God-fearing person is hyperbolically singled out for salvation, as though Paradise were created only for him.
KASHSHAF:92:17/r1.anchor: وجعل مختصا بالنجاة ،   كأن الجنة لم تخلق إلا له

KASHSHAF:92:17/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:17/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:17/r2.claim: One view identifies the most wretched as Abū Jahl or Umayya ibn Khalaf, and the most God-fearing as Abū Bakr.
KASHSHAF:92:17/r2.anchor: وقيل : هما أبو جهل أو أمية بن خلف

MAWARDI:92:15/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:15/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:92:15/r1.anchor: { لا يَصلاها إلا الأشْقَى } أي الشقّي .

NASAFI:92:15/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:15/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:15/r1.claim: Only the most wretched enters that Fire to remain there eternally.
NASAFI:92:15/r1.anchor: { لاَ يصلاها } لا يدخلها للخلود فيها { إِلاَّ الأشقى

NASAFI:92:18/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:18/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
NASAFI:92:18/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda reads “most wretched” as “wretched” (unbeliever) and “most pious” as “pious” (believer): the generic classes, not only the most extreme individuals, burn or are saved.
NASAFI:92:18/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : الأشقى بمعنى الشقي

NASAFI:92:18/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:18/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:18/r5.claim: Another view says the passage compares outstanding figures among polytheists and believers, speaking as if the Fire were made only for one and Paradise only for the other.
NASAFI:92:18/r5.anchor: وقيل : الآية واردة في الموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين وعظيم من المؤمنين

NASAFI:92:18/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:18/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:18/r6.claim: A reported identification makes the most wretched Abū Jahl and the most pious Abū Bakr.
NASAFI:92:18/r6.anchor: وقيل : هما أبو جهل وأبو بكر

NASAFI:92:18/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:18/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:18/r7.claim: Nasafī says these verses refute the Murjiʾite claim that only an unbeliever enters Hell.
NASAFI:92:18/r7.anchor: وفيه بطلان زعم المرجئة لأنهم يقولون لا يدخل النار إلا كافر

QURTUBI:92:15/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:15/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:15/r1.claim: To undergo the Fire means to experience its heat.
QURTUBI:92:15/r1.anchor: " لا يصلاها " أي لا يجد صلاها وهو حرها

QURTUBI:92:15/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:15/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:15/r2.claim: The most wretched one means the wretched person.

QURTUBI:92:16/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r4.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:92:16/r4.claim: Al-Farra says the wretched one is whoever was wretched in God's knowledge.
QURTUBI:92:16/r4.anchor: إلا من كان شقيا في علم اللّه جل ثناؤه

QURTUBI:92:16/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r5.speaker: ابن عباس عن الضحاك
QURTUBI:92:16/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, through al-Dahhak, identifies the wretched one with Umayya ibn Khalaf and those like him who denied Muhammad.
QURTUBI:92:16/r5.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال : " لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى " أمية بن خلف ونظراؤه

QURTUBI:92:16/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r10.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
QURTUBI:92:16/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the Murji'a use these verses to argue that only unbelievers enter the Fire.

QURTUBI:92:16/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r11.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
QURTUBI:92:16/r11.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects that inference: this is a particular Fire, while Hell has levels, including the hypocrites' lowest level, and God may punish with any threatened kind of torment.

QURTUBI:92:16/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r12.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
QURTUBI:92:16/r12.claim: Al-Zajjaj adds that God forgives sins short of associating partners for whomever He wills; otherwise that promise would have no meaning, so non-polytheists may still be punished.
QURTUBI:92:16/r12.anchor: وقال جل ثناؤه :  " إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به

QURTUBI:92:16/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI:92:16/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhshari sees a contrast between exemplary leaders among unbelievers and believers: each is described in the superlative as if the Fire or Garden were made for him alone.
QURTUBI:92:16/r13.anchor: الزمخشري : الآية واردة في الموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين وعظيم من المؤمنين

QURTUBI:92:16/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:16/r14.claim: One reported identification names Abu Jahl or Umayya ibn Khalaf as the wretched figure and Abu Bakr as the God-fearing figure.
QURTUBI:92:16/r14.anchor: وقيل : هما أبو جهل أو أمية بن خلف . وأبو بكر رضي اللّه عنه

QURTUBI:92:18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:18/r2.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
QURTUBI:92:18/r2.claim: Some semanticists say the forms atqa and ashqa mean pious and wretched; the Afʿal pattern can stand for faʿil, as in akbar meaning kabir and ahwan meaning hayyin, with Tarafa's poem illustrating the usage.
QURTUBI:92:18/r2.anchor: وقال بعض أهل المعاني : أراد بقوله " الأتقى " و " الأشقى " أي التقي والشقي ، كقول طرفة

RAZI:92:15/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:92:15/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the passage was revealed about Umayya ibn Khalaf and others who denied Muhammad and earlier prophets.
RAZI:92:15/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس : نزلت في أمية بن خلف وأمثاله الذين كذبوا محمدا والأنبياء قبله

RAZI:92:15/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:92:15/r2.claim: Al-Razi says al-ashqā can mean “wretched,” as in “not the one-and-only”; he explains the phrase as a disbeliever who rejects God's signs and turns from obedience.
RAZI:92:15/r2.anchor: وقيل : إن الأشقى بمعنى الشقي كما يقال : لست فيها بأوحد أي بواحد

RAZI:92:15/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r3.speaker: المرجئة
RAZI:92:15/r3.claim: The Murjiʾites use the passage to argue only unbelievers are threatened with punishment.
RAZI:92:15/r3.anchor: واعلم أن المرجئة يتمسكون بهذه الآية في أنه لا وعيد إلا على الكفار

RAZI:92:15/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r4.speaker: القاضي
RAZI:92:15/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues that the apparent restriction would keep from Hell an unbeliever who had not denied and turned away.
RAZI:92:15/r4.anchor: قال القاضي : ولا يمكن إجراء هذه الآية على ظاهرها ، ويدل على ذلك ثلاثة أوجه ( أحدها ) : أنه يقتضي أن لا يدخل النار

RAZI:92:15/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r5.speaker: القاضي
RAZI:92:15/r5.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues the restriction invites sin by assuring believers who did not deny or turn away that sin cannot harm them, virtually permitting it.
RAZI:92:15/r5.anchor: ( وثانيها ) : أن هذا إغراء بالمعاصي ، لأنه بمنزلة أن يقول الله تعالى : لمن صدق بالله ورسوله ولم يكذب ولم يتول

RAZI:92:15/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r8.speaker: القاضي
RAZI:92:15/r8.claim: Al-Qāḍī alternatively takes “blazing fire” as all Hell, but reads the restriction as saying the most wretched alone is most entitled to it.
RAZI:92:15/r8.anchor: ( الثاني ) : أن المراد بقوله : { نارا تلظى } النيران أجمع ، ويكون المراد بقوله : { لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى } أي هذا الأشقى به أحق

RAZI:92:15/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:92:15/r10.claim: Al-Razi rejects the charge of enticing sin: present disgrace and God's anger deter, and God may punish another way; punishment need not be limited to Hell.
RAZI:92:15/r10.anchor: لأنه يكفي في الزجر عن المعصية حصول الذم في العاجل وحصول غضب الله

RAZI:92:15/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:92:15/r13.claim: Al-Razi rejects the reading “more entitled” as abandoning the apparent sense without evidence.
RAZI:92:15/r13.anchor: وأما قوله : المراد إن هذا الأشقى أحق به فضعيف لأنه ترك للظاهر من غير دليل

RAZI:92:15/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r14.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI:92:15/r14.claim: Al-Wāḥidī explains lā yaṣlāhā as not remaining in the fire while enduring its heat: unbelievers remain there, whereas a sinful believer may avoid it or leave.
RAZI:92:15/r14.anchor: ( الأول ) : ما ذكره الواحدي وهو أن معنى : { لا يصلاها } لا يلزمها في حقيقة اللغة

RAZI:92:15/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:92:15/r15.claim: Al-Razi's other answer restricts the general wording by verses threatening sinful believers with punishment.
RAZI:92:15/r15.anchor: ( الثاني ) : أن يخص عموم هذا الظاهر بالآيات الدالة على وعيد الفساق

RAZI:92:16/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
